Axisymmetric waves of a homogeneous incompressible disk

Words: 269 Articles: 4
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
In a thin constant-density disk with free surfaces z=±H, neglect slow radial gradients and let perturbations vary as eikr−iωt. With h=p′/ρ, the local inviscid equations are −iωu−2Ωv=−ikh, −iωv+κ2u/(2Ω)=0, −iωw=−hz​ and iku+wz​=0. Eliminating velocity gives hzz​=k2ω2h/(ω2−κ2). This local WKB approximation assumes H/r≪1 and ∣kr∣≫1 and has both surface and inertial wave branches.

Energy identity for free-surface disk waves

Words: 52
Axisymmetric waves of a homogeneous incompressible disk OurBigBook.com
For radial and vertical Lagrangian fluid displacements of a local axisymmetric mode, integrate the momentum equations and use incompressible flow plus the free-surface pressure condition of an incompressible disk. The result is
ω2∫−HH​(∣ξr​∣2+∣ξz​∣2)dz=κ2∫−HH​∣ξr​∣2dz+Ωz2​H(∣ξz​(H)∣2+∣ξz​(−H)∣2).
(1)
For nonnegative κ2 and positive Ωz2​, every nontrivial oscillatory mode has real nonnegative ω2. The surface term is the gravitational restoring energy of the displaced vacuum interfaces.

Inertial modes of an incompressible disk

Words: 69
Axisymmetric waves of a homogeneous incompressible disk OurBigBook.com
For 0<ω2<κ2, set S=kHω/κ2−ω2​. Even-pressure modes satisfy ω2=−Ωz2​StanS, while odd-pressure modes satisfy ω2=Ωz2​ScotS. In the case Ωz​>κ>0, the branches approach κ as kH→0. For each fixed vertical order n≥1 and large kH, S→nπ/2 and ω∼κnπ/(2kH). Even orders have even pressure and odd orders odd pressure. The limiting boundary condition is zero normal derivative of pressure at both interfaces.

Axisymmetric waves of a homogeneous incompressible disk OurBigBook.com
For ω2>κ2, set Q=kHω/ω2−κ2​. Even-pressure and odd-pressure modes have p′∝cosh(Qz/H) and sinh(Qz/H) and obey ω2=Ωz2​QtanhQ and ω2=Ωz2​QcothQ, respectively. At large kH, both become free-surface gravity waves with
ω2∼21​[κ2+κ4+4Ωz4​(kH)2​]=Ωz2​kH+21​κ2+O((kH)−1).
(2)
Their opposite-parity splitting is exponentially small as the two interfaces decouple.

Free-surface pressure condition of an incompressible disk

Words: 41
Axisymmetric waves of a homogeneous incompressible disk OurBigBook.com
Vertical hydrostatic equilibrium gives p0​=ρΩz2​(H2−z2)/2. At a vacuum interface, the Lagrangian pressure perturbation vanishes: p′+ξz​∂z​p0​=0. The vertical equation gives ξz​=pz′​/(ρω2), hence
p′−ω2Ωz2​​zpz′​=0at z=±H.
(3)
The moving interface makes this different from setting the Eulerian perturbation of a fluid variable p′ to zero on the original surface.

Kuzmin disk (Σ(R)=mb/[2π(R2+b2)3/2])

Words: 219 Articles: 2
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
A Kuzmin disk is an infinitesimally thin axisymmetric astrophysical disk whose relative potential is ψ=Gm/R2+(∣z∣+b)2​, with m,b>0. Away from the disk this is a point-mass vacuum field. The jump of its vertical derivative is −2Gmb/(R2+b2)3/2, so the Poisson equation for Newtonian gravity, written ∇2ψ=−4πGρ, gives the displayed surface density. Integrating 2πRΣ gives total mass m.

Kuzmin reflection method (Σ(R)=−∂z​ψ(R,0+)/(2πG))

Words: 167 Articles: 1
Kuzmin disk OurBigBook.com
Reflect a vacuum gravitational potential in the upper half-space evenly across z=0. For the convention in which gravitational acceleration is ∇ψ, the derivative jump is 2∂z​ψ(R,0+)=−4πGΣ(R). Thus a point mass m below the plane produces a Kuzmin disk, and superposing point masses with weight μ(b)db produces Σ(R)=(2π)−1∫0∞​bμ(b)(R2+b2)−3/2db. Positive weights give a nonnegative surface density wherever the integral converges.

Scale-free Kuzmin superposition (μ(b)=Bbβ,0<β<1)

Words: 110
Kuzmin reflection method OurBigBook.com
For B>0 and 0<β<1, the unreferenced relative potential of the Kuzmin reflection method diverges at large b. Referencing each component to the origin before integrating gives the finite potential difference
ψ(R,z)=GB∫0∞​bβ[R2+(∣z∣+b)2​1​−b1​]db.
(4)
At small b the subtraction is integrable because β>0; at large b the difference is O(b−2), integrable because β<1. Its plane force is ∂R​ψ=−CRβ−1, where C=(GB/2)B((1+β)/2,1−β/2). A circular speed V=KRβ/2 fixes C=K2, giving
Σ(R)=2πGK2Rβ−1​Γ((1+β)/2)Γ(1−β/2)Γ(1+β/2)Γ((1−β)/2)​.
(5)
The beta function substitutions for the force and surface density have different exponents. Its central mass is locally finite, but its total mass diverges at large radius; a potential zero at infinity cannot be imposed. The force and density approach those of the Mestel disk as β↓0.

Disk warp (W(R)=β(R)eiγ(R))

Words: 196 Articles: 2
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
A disk warp is a radial change of the orbital plane of successive disk annuli. In the small-tilt approximation, a complex tilt W records its magnitude and azimuth. Pressure and internal torques communicate the tilt through bending waves of a Keplerian disk in the inviscid thin-disk regime. A flat tilted disk has constant W even though its absolute orientation differs from the reference equatorial plane.

Inviscid warp equations of a nearly Keplerian disk (ΣR2Ω(Wt​−iω1​W)=R−1GR​,Gt​−iω2​G=41​PR3ΩWR​)

Words: 137 Articles: 1
Disk warp OurBigBook.com
Here G is the complex internal horizontal torque, P the vertically integrated pressure, and ω1​,ω2​ the approximate nodal precession and apsidal precession rates. In the exactly Keplerian case, local plane waves obey ω2=k2P/(4Σ)=k2cs2​/4, so tilt disturbances propagate at cs​/2. The secular thin-disk approximation requires wavelengths large relative to the height while the local approximation requires them small relative to the orbital radius.

Stationary bending warp of a Kerr disk (W=W∞​cos(xin​−x)/cosxin​,x=424a​r−5/4/(5ϵ))

Words: 77
Inviscid warp equations of a nearly Keplerian disk OurBigBook.com
For a>0, Σ∝R−3/4, constant disk aspect ratio ϵ=H/R, and r=Rc2/(GM), the inviscid steady disk warp equation reduces to Wxx​+W=0 in the displayed coordinate. The vanishing inner torque gives Wx​(xin​)=0; the outer tilt gives W(0)=W∞​. The displayed solution holds when cosxin​=0. If xin​=π, it is W=W∞​cosx, with an aligned node at r=24/5rin​ and opposite signed inner tilt. For negative spin the corresponding equation is hyperbolic, giving W=W∞​cosh(xin​−x)/coshxin​ with x=424∣a∣​r−5/4/(5ϵ).

Hankel representation of thin-disk gravity (Φ=∫0∞​S(k)J0​(kR)e−k∣z∣dk)

Words: 40
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
For an axisymmetric reflection-symmetric thin disk, the Laplace equation in cylindrical coordinates separates into regular radial Bessel functions and vertical decaying exponentials. The divergence theorem imposes Φz+​−Φz−​=4πGΣ. Hankel transform inversion gives S(k)=−2πG∫0∞​Σ(R)J0​(kR)RdR. Its radial derivative gives the galaxy rotation curve. Infinite scale-free models may require subtracting an additive divergent constant.

Angular-momentum-conserving self-gravitating disc radius (Rh​/Rd​=Cd​fd​/q2)

Words: 55
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
Let a disc contain fraction fd​ of total halo mass, take its edge gravity to be vd2​=Cd​GMd​/Rd​, and equate its edge specific angular momentum to qRh​vvir​. With vvir2​=GMh​/Rh​, these conditions give Rh​/Rd​=Cd​fd​/q2. The structural coefficient Cd​ is essential: disc mass alone does not uniquely determine its edge rotation curve.

Protoplanetary disk

Words: 118 Articles: 2
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
A protoplanetary disk is a gas-and-solid astrophysical disk around a young star in which planet formation occurs. Its evolution combines accretion, radiation, gas dynamics and the growth of solid material. A minimum-mass solar nebula is one reconstruction of the material needed to form the Solar System.

Protoplanetary disk dispersal

Words: 37
Protoplanetary disk OurBigBook.com
Removal of disk gas by accretion onto the host star, winds and photoevaporation. The finite availability of gas limits which solid cores can acquire massive envelopes. The disk's evolutionary state matters more than a single universal dispersal time.

Snow line

Words: 42
Protoplanetary disk OurBigBook.com
A transition beyond which a specified volatile can predominantly condense into solid grains under local temperature and pressure. Without qualification it often means the water-ice transition. In a Cartesian frame rotating with an epicyclic guiding center, a small planar oscillation obeys x=Xcos(κt+χ) and y=−(2ΩX/κ)sin(κt+χ). The ellipse is elongated azimuthally when the radial epicyclic frequency satisfies κ<2Ω. Conservation of angular momentum makes the motion around the guiding centre retrograde.

Epicyclic guiding center (x0​)

Words: 41
Epicyclic motion OurBigBook.com
The epicyclic guiding center is the circular-orbit location about which a particle performs epicyclic motion. In a Keplerian shearing sheet, the conserved canonical momentum is py​=y˙​+2Ωx=Ωx0​/2. The guiding center therefore labels the particle's first-order specific angular momentum offset, even while its instantaneous radial coordinate oscillates.

Epicyclic energy (Eepi​)

Words: 31
Epicyclic motion OurBigBook.com
For epicyclic motion in a Keplerian shearing sheet, write x−x0​=Re(Ae−iΩt). The energy of the radial harmonic oscillator per unit mass is Eepi​=Ω2∣A∣2/2. The full horizontal Jacobi energy in a shearing sheet also includes the negative guiding-center term −3Ω2x02​/8.

Plasma beta (β)

Words: 13
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
Plasma beta is the ratio of gas pressure to magnetic pressure, β=Pg​/Pm​.

Sub-Keplerian rotation

Words: 160 Articles: 3
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
Sub-Keplerian rotation has angular speed below that of a circular Keplerian orbit at the same radius. In a gaseous disk, an outwardly decreasing pressure supplies some radial support and makes the gas sub-Keplerian.

Radial drift of solids in a gas disk (vpr​=−2ηvK​St/(1+St2))

Words: 85 Articles: 1
Sub-Keplerian rotation OurBigBook.com
For test particles with linear drag, negligible radial gas flow and negligible dust feedback, Sub-Keplerian rotation removes solid-particle angular momentum. The displayed inward velocity uses Stokes number St=ΩK​ts​ and the pressure-gradient parameter of a protoplanetary disk. Drift is fastest at St=1; the physical particle size at that point depends on the local gas and drag law.

Dust trap

Words: 39
Radial drift of solids in a gas disk OurBigBook.com
A region that concentrates solids by opposing their loss through radial drift. Near a radial gas-pressure maximum, the pressure-support drift changes sign and carries particles toward the maximum from both sides. Gas advection and turbulent diffusion can limit retention.

Pressure-gradient parameter of a protoplanetary disk (η=−21​(cs​/vK​)2dlnPg​/dlnr)

Words: 44
Sub-Keplerian rotation OurBigBook.com
A convention for the small fractional reduction of azimuthal gas speed due to radial pressure support. With cs2​=Pg​/ρg​, radial balance gives vgϕ2​=vK2​(1−2η) and hence vgϕ​≃vK​(1−η). Other authors absorb the factor of two into the definition; the convention must accompany a drift formula.

Streaming instability

Words: 61 Articles: 1
Astrophysical disk OurBigBook.com
The streaming instability is an instability of mutually coupled gas and solid particles in a disk. Relative drift and drag can concentrate the particles into dense structures.

Streaming instability resonance

Words: 34
Streaming instability OurBigBook.com
A streaming-instability resonance occurs when a gas wave has frequency ω=k⋅Δu, matching the wave phase to the particle drift. The resonant forcing then produces algebraic particle-density growth in the test-particle limit.
